title: McKown v. Simon Prop. Group Inc.
questions: Whether, in this action brought against a mall owner and a mall security firm by a store employee who was one of those shot during a third party’s criminal rampage, the plaintiff must show that similar violent acts previously occurred on the premises in order to establish that the defendants owed him a duty to protect him from the third party’s criminal acts.

title: Cornelius v. Dep't of Ecology
questions: Whether the Pollution Control Hearings Board correctly determined that the Department of Ecology did not violate the Washington Constitution or Revised Code when it approved Washington State University's applications to amend the water rights serving the Pullman campus

title: State of Washington v. Jones
questions: This case involves whether Leroy Jones's Florida convictions are comparable to a Washington "most serious offense" under the Sentencing Reform Act and whether defense counsel was ineffective when it failed to investigate two witnesses

title: State of Washington v. Blazina
questions: Did the Court of Appeals err when it declined to consider a challenge to the trial court's imposition of legal financial obligations (LFOs) where the challenge was raised for the first time on appeal?

title: Pub. Util. Dist. No. 1 of Okanogan County v. State of Washington
questions: The court considers whether public utility districts are authorized to condemn school lands and, if so, whether the particular school lands at issue in this case are exempt from condemnation either because they are held in trust or because they are dedicated to a particular use insofar as they are presently used for cattle grazing. The court also considers the propriety of Conservation Northwest's intervention in the case

title: State of Washington v. Condon
questions: Condon was charged, in the alternative, with first degree murder and felony murder. Was there sufficient evidence to convict him of first degree murder and was he entitled to a lesser included offense jury instruction on second degree murder?

title: State of Washington v. E.J.J.
questions: Did the defendant's conviction for obstruction of a police officer violate his free speech rights?

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Meirhofer
questions: The case concerns the sexually violent predator statute. The issue is whether the State establish a prima facie case for continued confinement when the sexually violent predator's diagnosis changed and his likelihood of re-offending decreased. If the answer is yes, may the individual seek relief through a personal restraint petition?

title: Utter v. Bldg. Indus. Ass'n of Wash.
questions: The court must decide whether a citizen suit to enforce Washington's Fair Campaign Practices Act is permitted in this case, and, if it is, whether the trial court erred by granting summary judgment to one of the parties

title: Henne v. City of Yakima
questions: RCW 4.24.525 provides that the target of a strategic lawsuit against public participation can file a special motion to strike the lawsuit and will be awarded penalties if the motion is successful. Is a city allowed to file a special motion to strike under that statute? If one party files a special motion to strike, can the other party make that motion moot by voluntarily amending the challenged claims?

title: Crystal Ridge Homeowners Ass'n v. City of Bothell
questions: The court must decide whether the dedication of an easement to Snohomish County included a drainage pipe buried in the easement, and whether the county was therefore responsible for maintaining the pipe

title: State of Washington v. Maynard
questions: Did the trial court properly dismiss charges due to prosecutorial delay and ineffective assistance of counsel, when the defendant turned 18 shortly after being charged and therefore lost the benefit of adjudication in juvenile court?

title: State of Washington v. Walker
questions: Should Walker's convictions be reversed based on prosecutorial misconduct, improper jury instructions, or ineffective assistance of counsel?

title: Filo Foods, LLC v. City of SeaTac
questions: The court considers whether the City of SeaTac's $15 minimum wage initiative, now codified as SMC 7.45 et seq, is enforceable at the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport and against various employers in light of various state and federal laws.

title: State of Washington v. Hayes
questions: Whether in a criminal prosecution the trial court may impose an exceptional sentence on an offender convicted as an accomplice on the basis the crime constituted a major economic offense.

title: State of Washington v. Allen
questions: First, does a prosecutor commit misconduct when he misstated the law to the jury? Second, can a defendant's sentence be increased based solely on the conduct of his accomplice?

title: Paetsch v. Spokane Dermatology Clinic, PS
questions: Paetsch was injured when a certified physician's assistant (PA-C) employed by the clinic performed cosmetic surgery, and when that PA-C later misdiagnosed her reaction to the surgery. title: State of Washington v. S.J.C.
questions: What are the standards that govern the sealing of juvenile records?

title: State of Washington v. Bruch
questions: The trial court sentenced the petitioner to a variable term of community custody: "At least four months, plus all accrued earned early release time at the time of release." The petitioner argues that he must receive a fixed term, no longer than four months

title: State of Washington v. Friedlund
questions: : For exceptional sentences, can the written findings requirement be satisfied by anything less than formal written findings of fact and conclusions of law signed by the trial court judge?

title: State of Washington v. Kalebaugh
questions: Whether comments made during juror orientation require reversal of the defendant's conviction

title: State of Washington v. Z. U. E.
questions: Whether the information provided by multiple 911 callers has sufficient 'indicia of reliability,' to justify an officer's investigatory stop of a car to investigate a suspicion of criminal activity

title: J.S. v. Vill. Voice Media Holdings, LLC
questions: A federal statute, the Communications Decency Act of 1996, 47 U.S.C. § 230(c)(1) (CDA), immunizes certain interactive computer service providers from liability for content that other content providers post on the publisher's website. In this case, the minor plaintiff-respondents allege that pimps advertised them for sale as prostitutes on the appellants' website. Adult customers allegedly responded to these ads and raped the respondents. Does the CDA provide Backpage with immunity from liability for J.S.'s state law claims?

title: In re Welfare of A.W.
questions: There are two issues presented in this direct review case: (1) whether the preponderance of the evidence standard of proof to establish a guardianship under chapter 13.36 RCW satisfies due process; and (2) whether there is substantial evidence in the record to support the trial court's decision to establish guardianship for A.W. and M.W.

title: State of Washington v. Barry
questions: Whether a fifth or sixth amendment violation occurs when a trial court instructs the jury that it may consider the defendant's courtroom demeanor as evidence

title: In Re Pers. Restraint of Yung-Cheng Tsai
questions: Are the petitioners allowed to withdraw their guilty pleas if their attorneys did not advise them of the immigration consequences of their convictions?

title: Worthington v. WestNET
questions: Whether the multijurisdictional, multiagency drug task force, WestNET, is an "agency" subject to suit under the Public Records Act

title: State of Washington v. Henderson
questions: The defendant was convicted of first degree murder by extreme indifference to human life. Should the jury have been given the option of convicting him of manslaughter?

title: State of Washington v. Glasmann
questions: The trial court instructed the jury that it may convict the defendant of a lower-degree crime if the jurors are unable to agree on a higher-degree crime. When the jury leaves the higher-degree verdict form blank but convicts the defendant of a lower-degree crime, do the state and federal double jeopardy clauses prohibit the defendant from later being retried on the higher-degree charge?

title: League of Women Voters of Wash. v. State of Washington
questions: Does Initiative 1240 (Charter Schools Act), codified in chapter 28A.710 RCW, violate various provisions of Washington's Constitution?

title: Ass'n of Wash. Spirits & Wine Distribs. v. Liquor Control Bd.
questions: The State Liquor Control Board imposed a $104.7 million shortfall fee on licensed spirits distributors. The court must decide whether Initiative 1183 required the Board to impose any part of the shortfall fee on distillers distributing their own spirits.

title: Predisik v. Spokane Sch. Dist. No. 81
questions: This is a Public Records Act case asking if disclosure of records would violate the privacy rights of two school district employees

title: State of Washington v. Fuentes
questions: Under the totality of circumstances, did reasonable suspicion of criminal activity support the Terry stop of the defendants in these consolidated cases?

title: State of Washington v. Sandholm
questions: Sandholm was convicted of felony DUI. Was Sandholm's right to a unanimous jury violated? Should Sandholm's prior drug offenses be included in his offender score?

title: Wash. Fed. v. Harvey
questions: The Harveys and the Gentrys guarantied certain commercial loans. Does the Deeds of Trust Act protect them from deficiency judgments when they did not pledge their own property?

title: State of Washington v. Brush
questions: Whether one of the jury instructions given at Brian Brush's trial was an improper comment on the evidence and whether certain hearsay testimony was improperly admitted

title: State of Washington v. Gomez
questions: Whether the trial judge affected a closure of the courtroom when he commented that no members of the public would be allowed to enter once the proceedings began

title: State of Washington v. Peeler
questions: Whether the State violated the Intrastate Detainers Act, chapter 9.98 RCW, by not bringing the defendant to trial within 120 days.

title: Davis v. Cox
questions: The court will consider the interpretation and constitutionality of the Washington Act Limiting Strategic Lawsuits Against Public Participation, RCW 4.24.525

title: State of Washington v. Carson
questions: Whether a defendant received ineffective assistance of counsel because his defense counsel successfully objected to a proposed instruction that the jurors must unanimously agree which alleged criminal action constitutes the crime charged (a Petrich instruction)

title: Jewels v. City Of Bellingham
questions: Under RCW 4.24.210(4)(a), a landowner may be liable "for injuries sustained to [land] users by reason of a known dangerous artificial latent condition for which warning signs have not been conspicuously posted." For a condition to be "known" under that statute, must the landowner know that it is both dangerous and latent?

title: W. Plaza, LLC v. Tison
questions: In a lease for a mobile home lot, is a provision limiting the amount and frequency of rent increases enforceable?

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Pfefer
questions: Should this court adopt the WSBA Disciplinary Board's unanimous recommendation that Pfefer be suspended for six months and pay restitution for failing to diligently pursue his client's case, failing to inform her about the status of her case, and improperly withdrawing from representation?

title: State of Washington v. Reis
questions: The governor vetoed a section of a 2011 bill that would have established a registry for medical users of marijuana. She did not veto another section that would have decriminalized use of marijuana by medical users who recorded their medical use with the vetoed registry. Did the remaining references to the registry survive the veto, with the result that medical use of marijuana remains criminal unless the user proves an affirmative defense of authorized use?

title: Gamboa v. Clark
questions: Can the Gamboas continue using their neighbor's driveway as they have for many years?

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Khan
questions: Whether the Acting Chief Judge at the Court of Appeals issued an order in violation of former RAP 16.11(b) and whether trial counsel was ineffective for (1) failing to provide an English language interpreter, (2) failing to object to alleged prosecutorial misconduct, or (3) failing to investigate and present expert witness testimony

title: Boeing Co. v. Dep't of Labor & Indus.
questions: Under the Industrial Insurance Act, is a self-insured employer entitled to relief from the second injury fund to cover the cost of a worker's post-pension medical treatment costs?

title: Keck v. Collins
questions: This case presents two issues. First, in a medical malpractice case, did the nonmoving party's expert provide sufficient facts to defeat summary judgment? Second, should an appellate court review de novo an order granting a motion to strike an untimely affidavit at summary judgment?

title: State of Washington v. Shale
questions: Can the State prosecute an enrolled member of the Yakama Nation living on the Quinault Indian Tribe's reservation for failing to register as a sex offender with the local county sheriff?

title: Save Our Scenic Area v. Skamania County
questions: Whether the plaintiffs' claims under the Growth Management Act and Planning Enabling Act were properly dismissed as time barred

title: State of Washington v. Besola
questions: Was evidence in this case seized under an overbroad warrant and did the jury instructions omit an essential element of the crime?

title: McCarthy Fin., Inc. v. Premera
questions: Whether the filed rate doctrine bars claims that health insurance providers violated Washington's Consumer Protection Act by making false and misleading representations

title: State of Washington v. Reeder
questions: Were subpoenas duces tecum issued by a Special Inquiry Judge for Reeder's bank records pursuant to RCW 10.27.170 invalid because they were not based on probable cause? Does Reeder's sentence violate principles of double jeopardy?

title: Queen Anne Park Homeowners Ass'n v. State Farm Fire & Cas. Co.
questions: What does "collapse" mean in an insurance policy that does not define the term?

title: Darkenwald v. Emp't Sec. Dep't
questions: Can the Employment Security Act's protections for part-time workers provide a presently employed worker with good cause to voluntarily leave her job?

title: Cannabis Action Council v. City of Kent
questions: Whether the Medical Use of Cannabis Act preempts a City of Kent ordinance

title: State of Washington v. Wheeler
questions: Defendants have one year to challenge their criminal convictions, subject to only a few limited exceptions. Does one of these exceptions provide a basis for Wheeler to bring a claim more than a year after he pleaded guilty?

title: Citizens All. for Prop. Rights Legal Fund v. San Juan County
questions: The Open Public Meetings Act applies to the San Juan County Council and to "any committee thereof when the committee acts on [its] behalf." RCW 42.30.020(2). When does a group qualify as a committee of the Council? When does a committee act on the Council's behalf?

title: State of Washington v. Love
questions: When the trial court heard for-cause juror challenges at a sidebar, did this violate the defendant's right to a public trial?

title: Maziar v. Dep't of Corr.
questions: Does the State have a right to a jury trial in tort actions against it?

title: State of Washington v. Gentry
questions: This case presents two issues. First, should the trial judge have recused herself? Second, after a court grants a motion for post-conviction DNA testing, what standard should a court apply when a party moves to end further DNA testing?

title: Lopez Demetrio v. Sakuma Bros. Farms
questions: Does a Washington agricultural employer have an obligation under Washington's Minimum Wage Act, or other state regulations, to pay piece-rate workers for rest breaks? If the answer is "yes," how must Washington agricultural employers calculate the rate of pay for the rest break time?

title: State of Washington v. O'Dell
questions: In a trial for second degree child rape, did the trial court properly decline to instruct the jury on the defendant's affirmative defense that he reasonably believed the victim was older? Did the trial court properly decline to consider the defendant's youth as a mitigating factor at sentencing, when the defendant committed his offense ten days after his 18th birthday?

title: State of Washington v. Figeroa Martines
questions: The defendant was convicted of DUI. This case concerns two issues. First, whether a warrant authorizing a blood draw from a DUI suspect implicitly authorizes testing that blood. Second, whether there was probable cause to test the defendant's blood for drugs and alcohol.

title: City of Seattle v. Evans
questions: Whether Evans' conviction under Seattle Municipal Code 12A.14.080, which prohibits carrying a fixed-blade knife in public, violated Evans' right to bear arms under article I, section 24 of the Washington State Constitution or the Second Amendment to the United States Constitution

title: State of Washington v. Hardtke
questions: Hardtke was required to wear an alcohol monitoring bracelet while awaiting trial. Does the court have the authority to impose the costs for the monitoring?

title: In re the Personal Restraint Petition of
questions: The court must determine whether the DOC had the authority to impose community custody conditions on Montgomery and whether the DOC-imposed conditions violated Montgomery's fundamental rights."

title: Gorre v. City of Tacoma
questions: Concerns statutory presumption that firefighters with certain injuries are entitled to workers' compensation benefits

title: Auto. United Trades Org. v. State of Washington
questions: The state and many Indian tribes have entered into fuel tax agreements. Do the agreements violate the constitution?

title: State of Washington v. Brock
questions: Whether the warrantless search of Brock's backpack constituted a lawful search incident to arrest or alternatively, a lawful inventory search.

title: State of Washington v. Ozuna
questions: The court will consider whether sufficient evidence exists to uphold the defendant's conviction for intimidation of a witness under RCW 9A.72.110(2)

title: Grant County Prosecuting Att'y v. Jasman
questions: May a person who is disqualified from being a public officer be employed as a public officer's deputy or employee?

title: State of Washington v. Davila
questions: The State failed to disclose, before trial, that one of the scientists who handled evidence used to convict the defendant had been fired for incompetence. Does this failure entitle the defendant to a new trial?

title: In re Det. of Reyes
questions: (1) Does a trial court commit structural error when a proceeding in a civil case is closed without justification? (2) Does a party to a civil case have standing to assert the constitutional rights of the general public?

title: In re Dependency of M.H.P.
questions: Can a court seal motions and orders in parental termination cases without providing notice to opposing parties?

title: State of Washington v. Herron
questions: (1) Did the defendant validly waive his right to a public trial? (2) Does a criminal defendant have standing to assert the constitutional rights of the general public?

title: In re Adoption of M.S.M.-P.
questions: Petitioner challenges the termination of his parental rights because the termination hearing was closed to the public

title: State of Washington v. Conover
questions: Whether RCW 9.94A.533(6) requires the sentencing court to run multiple school bus stop sentence enhancements imposed on multiple counts consecutively to each other

title: In re Estate of Jepsen
questions: Did the Court of Appeals correctly hold that this will contest action should be allowed to proceed?

title: SARA FOSTER v. WASHINGTON STATE DEPARTMENT OF
questions: Public waters have established minimum water levels. May the Department of Ecology approve a water permit that will impact these minimum water levels?

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Abele
questions: Should attorney Kathryn Abele be suspended from the practice of law for one year as a sanction for two separate violations of the lawyer Rules of Professional Conduct?

title: Wash. State Hosp. Ass'n v. Dep't of Health
questions: A Department of Health rule interprets "sale, purchase, or lease" to mean all changes of control. Is the rule valid?

title: Nw. Wholesale, Inc. v. Pac Organic Fruit, LLC
questions: Whether federal Bankruptcy Law (11 U.S.C. Sections 541(c)(1) and 365(e)(1)) preempts RCW 25.15.130(1)(d)'s provision dissociating a member of a limited liability company upon such member's filing a bankruptcy petition

title: State of Washington v. Hampton
questions: When a defendant asks to delay trial in order to change attorneys, may a judge consider the defendant's reasons for changing attorneys?

title: Rose v. Anderson Hay & Grain Co.
questions: Whether the administrative remedies available under the Commercial Motor Vehicle Safety Act preclude the plaintiff from recovery under the tort for wrongful discharge in violation of public policy.

title: Rickman v. Premera Blue Cross
questions: Rickman sued her former employer for wrongful discharge. The court must decide whether she can proceed to trial

title: Becker v. Cmty. Health Sys., Inc..
questions: Whether a claim of wrongful discharge in violation of public policy should be dismissed because the plaintiff cannot satisfy the jeopardy element

title: State of Washington v. Mayer
questions: Whether a police officer's responses to a suspect's questions about the appointment of counsel undermined the Miranda warnings

title: Steven Klein, Inc. v. Dep't of Revenue
questions: Is money that a car dealership receives from the manufacturer through a "dealer cash" sales incentive program taxable?

title: Filmore, LLLP v. Unit Owners Ass'n of Centre Pointe Condo.
questions: Does an amendment to a condominium declaration restricting leasing require 67% or 90% approval?

title: Brown v. Dep't of Commerce
questions: Concerns the scope of the exemption from the Foreclosure Fairness Act's mediation program under RCW 61.24.166.

title: State of Washington v. Fedorov
questions: Concerns the right to private consultation with counsel under CrR 3.1, the rule-based right to counsel

title: Trujillo v. Nw. Tr. Servs., Inc.
questions: (1) Did NWTS breach its duty of good faith by relying upon a beneficiary declaration stating that the declarant "is the actual holder of the promissory note or other obligation evidencing the above-referenced loan or has requisite authority under RCW 62A.3-301 to enforce said obligation," when NWTS allegedly had reason to know that the declarant was not the owner of the note? (2) If yes, does Trujillo state claims for violations of the Criminal Profiteering Act and the CPA, and for intentional infliction of emotional distress?

title: State of Washington v. Beaver
questions: Whether revoking an insanity acquittee's conditional release without a judicial finding that the acquittee currently suffers from a mental illness violates procedural or substantive due process

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Moi
questions: Does double jeopardy bar trying a man for murder after he was acquitted of possessing the gun that killed the victim?

title: State of Washington v. Thurlby
questions: Whether the trial court violated Thurlby's right to be present at trial when it found that Thurlby was voluntarily absent and completed the second day of Thurlby's two-day jury trial in her absence

title: Thornell v. Seattle Serv. Bureau, Inc.
questions: Whether a non-resident may sue a Washington Corporation under the Washington Consumer Protection Act

title: State of Washington v. Larson
questions: Whether wire cutters are a "device designed to overcome security systems" under the retail theft statute.

In re Pers. Restraint of Erhart
Kitsap County Deputy Sheriffs' Guild v. Kitsap County
